title: Harvey is raising at $15.5bn, up 40% in five months
excerpt: Legal AI startup Harvey is in talks to raise $500m at a $15.5bn valuation, up 40% in five months, on $350m in annualised revenue.
content_html:
The legal-AI startup is in talks to raise at least $500m at a $15.5bn valuation, including the new money, The Information reported. That is a 40% jump on the $11bn it set only five months ago, when it raised $200m. Lightspeed Venture Partners is keen to lead the round.

The raise follows a revenue surge. Harvey, founded four years ago, now makes more than $350m in annualised revenue, up over 80% from $190m in January. At $15.5bn, that values the company at roughly 44 times its current revenue run rate. It is a price that assumes the growth keeps coming.

Vertical AI is having a moment

Harvey is the poster child for vertical AI, software built for one profession rather than everyone. The bet is that a tool trained on contracts, filings and case law beats a general chatbot for legal work. Its numbers suggest lawyers agree, and rivals such as Legora are chasing the same market.

The momentum runs past the funding line. In recent weeks Harvey took strategic investment from Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, deepened a partnership with Microsoft, and won firmwide deployments at big law firms. It is trying to become plumbing, not a plug-in.

The bull case, and the risk

The timing is striking. Investors are fleeing public software in what the market calls the SaaSpocalypse, the fear AI will hollow out subscription firms. Yet they keep pouring record sums into private AI. Harvey is the counter-example. The legal incumbents feel the shift too, with Thomson Reuters cutting engineers as it rebuilds around AI.

The real risk sits one layer down. Harvey rents its intelligence from model makers like OpenAI and Anthropic, the same firms whose tools could one day do the job directly. App builders such as Cursor have already felt the squeeze when a model owner changed terms. A 44-times multiple leaves little room if that pressure lands.

For now, the money is voting yes. A four-year-old company is worth more than most listed software firms, on the strength of a product lawyers did not know they wanted two years ago. Whether $15.5bn proves a bargain or a peak is the bet its next backers must place.

content_html_zh:
据 The Information 报道，这家合法的人工智能初创公司正在洽谈融资至少 5 亿美元，估值为 155 亿美元，其中包括新资金。 这比 5 个月前筹集 2 亿美元时设定的 110 亿美元增长了 40%。 Lightspeed Venture Partners 热衷于领投此轮融资。

此次加薪是在收入激增之后进行的。 Harvey 成立于四年前，目前年化收入超过 3.5 亿美元，比 1 月份的 1.9 亿美元增长了 80% 以上。 该公司的估值为 155 亿美元，约为当前收入运行率的 44 倍。 这是一个假设经济持续增长的价格。

垂直人工智能正在风靡一时

Harvey 是垂直人工智能的典型代表，这种软件是为某一职业而不是所有人而构建的。 我们的赌注是，经过合同、文件和判例法训练的工具在法律工作方面会击败一般的聊天机器人。 其数据表明律师们也同意这一观点，而 Legora 等竞争对手也在追逐同一市场。

势头已经超过了资金线。 最近几周，哈维获得了高盛和摩根大通的战略投资，加深了与微软的合作关系，并赢得了大型律师事务所的全公司部署。 它试图成为管道，而不是插件。

牛市情况和风险

时机非常惊人。 投资者正在逃离市场所谓的 SaaS 末日的公共软件，他们担心人工智能会掏空订阅公司。 然而，他们却不断向私人人工智能领域投入创纪录的资金。 哈维就是一个反例。 现任法律公司也感受到了这种转变，汤森路透在围绕人工智能进行重建时裁减了工程师。

真正的风险位于下面一层。 Harvey 从 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等模型制造商那里租用情报，这些公司的工具有一天可以直接完成这项工作。 当模型所有者更改条款时，Cursor 等应用程序构建者已经感受到了压力。 如果压力下降，44 倍的市盈率就几乎没有空间了。

目前，资金投了赞成票。 一家成立四年的公司的价值超过了大多数上市软件公司，因为其产品律师在两年前还不知道他们想要什么。 155 亿美元到底是便宜还是顶峰，是其下一个支持者必须下的赌注。
